attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, endorsed.

semantics.note: The normalisation captures both parts: the transparency criticism and the requirement to enter credentials through a remote VM. It doesn't add claims about password storage.

contract.note: Fair, ordinary reading. It ties transparency to the founder-history passage and treats 'any service' as any supported service. The broad transparency judgment has no standard, so its result depends on the evaluator's interpretation.

evidence.note: WIRED's launch-period review (May 3, 2024) directly describes a VNC session where users type in their service logins. This supports the login part only.

Rabbit's own January 2024 statement that it doesn't store credentials. It qualifies a storage reading but doesn't contradict that credentials are entered. It is a company disclosure, not an independent finding.

Cointelegraph reports Rabbit's response that the rebrand was disclosed in 2023. This is a company statement, published before the cutoff. It doesn't establish full disclosure, and the 2023 event_date refers to the cited article, not this report.

reviews.rationale: The login part is supported: WIRED's launch-period review confirms credentials are typed into a remote VNC session. The transparency part is not settled. The packet has no independent record of specific omissions or conflicting disclosures, and Rabbit's claimed 2023 rebrand disclosure rebuts only part of it. The support condition needs both parts and the contradiction condition is not met, so the claim is unresolved overall.
